verdict.root_cause: Not established. The evidence in hand shows a partial, bursty failure: frontend's error ratio oscillates between 0% and ~10.7% and productcatalogservice's between 0% and ~12% over the same window, with both services continuously serving and continuously emitting telemetry (tr_4ebe6206b86b, tr_daca9f7e265e, tr_12e2b1ea0143). No change of any kind — deploy, config push, or flag flip — is recorded for either frontend or productcatalogservice in the 15 minutes bracketing onset (tr_3b5877322382, tr_05b147cb267b, tr_969733dc3889), which removes the simplest explanation without supplying a replacement. Every attempt to read productcatalogservice logs failed on a label-selector mismatch ("product-catalog-service" vs "productcatalogservice") and returned zero lines, so no failure signature — internal fault versus downstream timeout — was ever recovered (tr_3eab28a379bb, tr_94c6b6cd6baf). No latency series, no saturation or resource metrics, and no per-dependency breakdown were collected anywhere, and ten of the twelve services in the blast radius — including checkoutservice, which alerted 15 seconds after the others — were never dispatched to at all. The shape of the failure (intermittent bursts, no proximate change, culprit possibly unnamed by the page) is consistent with the ad-memory-squeeze pattern in the corpus, but that is a resemblance, not a finding: nothing here measured memory, threads, connections, or latency on any service.
verdict.reasoning: Two independent frontend metric dispatches agree the failure is partial and intermittent, not a hard outage, and both explicitly state they carry only a service_name dimension and therefore cannot attribute errors to any downstream (tr_4ebe6206b86b, tr_daca9f7e265e). The productcatalogservice error series shows the same bursty shape with a zero floor and a ~12% peak while the denominator stays non-zero, so that service was up and mostly succeeding (tr_12e2b1ea0143). Correlation of the two series is suggestive but untested — tr_daca9f7e265e says so directly. Three change dispatches returned empty logs for both services (tr_3b5877322382, tr_05b147cb267b, tr_969733dc3889), which is why I do not select bad_deploy, bad_config, or a rollback/config_revert remediation: a change record is the evidence that would support those classes and there is none, though two of those dispatches also note they covered only 15 of the 60 minutes asked about and were scoped by service name, so a platform-level or older change is unexamined rather than excluded. dependency_latency cannot be selected because no latency was measured at any hop — tr_4ebe6206b86b states there is no latency signal in its data at all. resource_exhaustion is the pattern the retrieved ad-memory-squeeze incident matched, and the symptom shape here rhymes with it, but no dispatch measured memory, CPU, file descriptors, connections, or threads on any service, so choosing it would be importing the corpus's answer rather than reading this incident's evidence. The log dispatches that would have named a failure signature both failed on a selector mismatch and are correctly self-flagged as such (tr_3eab28a379bb, tr_94c6b6cd6baf) — their emptiness is a tooling artifact and is not evidence of silence from the service. With the mechanism unidentified, no remediation can be named honestly; restarting or scaling on this basis would be a guess.
